name: The five activities of the mind (pañca vṛttayaḥ)

definitions.definition: Valid cognition (pramāṇa: perception, inference, testimony), error (viparyaya), conceptual construction (vikalpa), sleep (nidrā) and memory (smṛti), each afflicted (kliṣṭa) or unafflicted (akliṣṭa) (YS 1.5–1.11). Afflicted ones are caused by the afflictions and become the field for the karma-store; unafflicted ones have discernment as object; the two arise in each other's gaps; activities and impressions produce each other in an unceasing wheel (YBh 1.5). All of them are of the nature of pleasure, pain and delusion, and are to be stilled (YBh 1.11).

relations.note: afflicted activities are caused by the afflictions (YBh 1.5)

name: The five afflictions (kleśa)

definitions.definition: Ignorance, I-am-ness, attachment, aversion and clinging to life (YS 2.3), which Vyāsa calls the five errors (viparyaya) (YBh 2.3, 1.8); ignorance is the field of the rest, each of which may be dormant, attenuated, interrupted or fully active (YS 2.4). They are the root of the karma-store (YS 2.12) and are thinned by kriyā-yoga (YS 2.2).

relations.note: they are the root of the afflicted activities and of the karma-store

name: The states of the afflictions (dormant, attenuated, interrupted, fully active)

definitions.definition: Prasupta (dormant), tanu (attenuated), vicchinna (interrupted), udāra (fully active) (YS 2.4). Vyāsa: dormancy is the seed-state of bare potency awakened by facing a support; attenuation is by the cultivation of the opposite; interruption is acting again and again in this or that form (anger absent at a time of passion); fully active is having gained activity toward an object; he adds a fifth, the burnt-seed (dagdha-bīja) state, in the one of the last body (YBh 2.4).

name: The levels of the mind (citta-bhūmi)

definitions.definition: Scattered (kṣipta), stupefied (mūḍha), distracted (vikṣipta), one-pointed (ekāgra) and stilled (niruddha) (YBh 1.1). Samādhi in a distracted mind, subordinate to distraction, does not count as yoga; in the one-pointed mind the samādhi that illumines the real object, wears away the afflictions and loosens karma's bonds is samprajñāta yoga; in the stilling of all activities it is asamprajñāta (YBh 1.1).

name: The four conditions of the mind's sattva (YBh 1.2)

definitions.definition: Vyāsa: the mind has three guṇas; its sattva, whose form is illumination, mixed with rajas and tamas is fond of lordship and sense-objects; pierced by tamas it goes toward adharma, ignorance, non-dispassion and non-lordship; when the covering of delusion is worn away and only touched by rajas it goes toward dharma, knowledge, dispassion and lordship; freed even of the trace of rajas it is established in its own form, reduced to discernment of the difference of sattva and puruṣa, and goes to the meditation of the cloud of dharma (YBh 1.2).

name: The four attitudes (maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā)

definitions.definition: Friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous, equanimity toward the non-virtuous, cultivated to make the mind clear (YS 1.33, YBh 1.33).

name: The three kinds of pain (duḥkha) named in YBh 1.31

definitions.definition: Relating to oneself (ādhyātmika), to other beings (ādhibhautika) and to the divine (ādhidaivika): that by which beings are struck and strive to strike it down (YBh 1.31). (Distinct from the three sufferings of transformation, anxiety and impression at YS 2.15.)

name: Everything is suffering for the discerning (YS 2.15)

definitions.definition: For the discerning (vivekin) everything is suffering, because of the suffering of transformation (pariṇāma), of anxiety (tāpa) and of impression (saṃskāra), and because of the conflict of the functions of the guṇas (YS 2.15). Vyāsa: the yogin is the eyeball on which a strand of wool troubles, and the ordinary person is not so troubled (YBh 2.15); only suffering not yet come is to be avoided (YS 2.16, YBh 2.16).

relations.note: the fourfold scheme of what is to be abandoned

name: The fourfold scheme of the śāstra (heya, heya-hetu, hāna, hānopāya)

definitions.definition: Saṃsāra full of suffering (what is to be abandoned), the conjunction of pradhāna and puruṣa (its cause), the absolute ceasing of the conjunction (the abandonment) and right seeing (the means): the śāstra is fourfold as the science of healing is fourfold (disease, cause, health, medicine) (YBh 2.15). Also named as heya (YS 2.16), heya-hetu (YS 2.17), hāna (YS 2.25) and hānopāya (YS 2.26).

name: The wearing away of the afflictions (kleśa-kṣaya)

definitions.definition: The afflictions are thinned by kriyā-yoga (YS 2.2), made like burnt seeds by discerning insight (YBh 2.2), abandoned in gross form by meditation and in subtle form by involution (YS 2.10–2.11); insight-born impressions cause their wearing away (YBh 1.50); with them worn away, karma no longer ripens (YBh 2.13).

name: The eight limbs of yoga (aṣṭāṅga)

definitions.definition: Restraints (yama), observances (niyama), posture (āsana), breath-regulation (prāṇāyāma), sense-withdrawal (pratyāhāra), concentration (dhāraṇā), meditation (dhyāna), samādhi (YS 2.29). By practising them impurity is destroyed and the light of knowledge rises to discernment (YS 2.28, YBh 2.28). Pāda 2 (this chunk) gives yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma and pratyāhāra (2.30–2.55); the last three follow in pāda 3.

name: Dispassion, lower and higher

definitions.definition: Lower: the consciousness of mastery in one free of thirst for seen and heard-of objects (YS 1.15); higher: freedom from thirst for the guṇas from knowing the puruṣa (YS 1.16); Vyāsa: the higher is only the clearness of knowledge, and kaivalya is inseparable from it (YBh 1.16).

name: Practice and dispassion (abhyāsa and vairāgya)

definitions.definition: By practice and dispassion the activities of the mind are stilled (YS 1.12); Vyāsa: the mind is a river flowing both ways; dispassion dries the stream toward objects, the practice of seeing discernment opens the stream of discernment (YBh 1.12).

name: Grades of practitioners (mṛdu, madhya, adhimātra)

definitions.definition: Vyāsa: by the means, nine kinds of yogin — mild, middling, intense means, each with mild, middling or intense ardor (saṃvega) — and further distinctions; the samādhi and its fruit is nearest for the intense (YS 1.21–1.22, YBh 1.20–1.22).

name: The five means: faith, energy, mindfulness, samādhi, insight

definitions.definition: For yogins samādhi is preceded by faith, energy, mindfulness, samādhi and insight (YS 1.20); Vyāsa: each arises from the previous — faith (serenity of mind, protecting the yogin like a kind mother), energy, mindfulness, concentration of the unagitated mind, and the discernment of insight by which one knows the thing as it is (YBh 1.20).

name: The sevenfold final insight (saptadhā prānta-bhūmi prajñā)

definitions.definition: Vyāsa: four belong to the liberation of insight (what is to be abandoned is fully known; its causes are worn away; abandonment is realised by the samādhi of stilling; the means, discernment, is cultivated) and three to the liberation of the mind (the buddhi's office is done; the guṇas dissolve into their cause; there is no further arising) (YS 2.27, YBh 2.27).

name: The levels of the guṇas (guṇa-parvan)

definitions.definition: Particularized (viśeṣa: five elements, ten faculties, mind), unparticularized (aviśeṣa: five tanmātras and I-am-ness alone), mere mark (liṅga-mātra: the great principle) and unmarked (aliṅga: the primal, pradhāna) (YS 2.19, YBh 2.19).

name: Kriyā-yoga, the yoga of action

definitions.definition: Austerity, self-study and devotion to Īśvara (YS 2.1), for cultivating samādhi and thinning the afflictions (YS 2.2); taught for the practitioner whose mind is not yet concentrated (YBh 2.1).

name: Signs of establishment in the restraints and observances

definitions.definition: YS 2.35–2.45: hostility abandoned; actions and fruits rest on the practitioner; jewels present themselves; vigour gained; understanding of the how of births; disgust for one's own body; purity of sattva and the rest; unsurpassed happiness; perfection of body and senses; union with the chosen deity; perfection of samādhi. The text's own descriptions; not promises to the reader.

name: Cultivating the opposite (pratipakṣa-bhāvanā)

definitions.definition: Against harmful thoughts (YS 2.33–2.34): contemplate the unwanted ripening that follows them (unending suffering and ignorance) and recall the refuge taken in the dharma of yoga (YBh 2.33, 2.34). Also how the afflictions are attenuated (YBh 2.4).

name: The five restraints (yama)

definitions.definition: Non-harming, truthfulness, non-stealing, continence, non-possessiveness (YS 2.30); the great vow when not limited by birth, place, time or occasion (YS 2.31). Non-harming is their root (YBh 2.30).

name: The five observances (niyama)

definitions.definition: Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study, devotion to Īśvara (YS 2.32).
